routes.name: Visa-free entry (no tourist card)
routes.summary: Citizens of Argentina, Chile, South Korea, Ecuador, Israel, Japan, Peru and Uruguay can enter without a visa or a tourist card. The official list does not state the maximum stay.

other: Maximum days of stay not stated on the page we read. Check with the DGM or a consulate before you go.
Passport must be valid for at least six months.

sources.label: MIREX consulate: country list and visa conditions

routes.name: Tourist card entry
routes.summary: Citizens of 146 countries and territories, including the US, Canada, Mexico, Spain, Germany and Brazil, enter for tourism with just a tourist card. People who can legally enter the EU, US, Canada or UK can also use it. Business trips need a business visa.

other: Applies to nationals of the 146 countries on the official tourist card list, for tourism only.
Also open to people with permanent residence or a valid multiple-entry visa for the US, EU (Schengen), Canada or the UK (Decree 691-07).

Passport valid for at least six months. DGM has waived this six-month rule for some nationalities (Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, US, England, EU) from Dec 1, 2025 to Dec 31, 2026.

fees.label: Tourist card (usually included in airfare, can be bought at the airport)

sources.label: MIREX consulate: country list and visa conditions

routes.name: Tourist Visa (TS / TM)
routes.summary: Citizens of about 102 countries, including China, India, Cuba, Haiti, Nigeria, Egypt and Vietnam, need a visa for tourism. Simple is one entry, multiple is two entries, both valid 60 days. Apply at a Dominican consulate.

other: Required for nationals of the countries in Section D of the official list. Skip it if you hold permanent residence or a valid multiple-entry visa for the US, EU (Schengen), Canada or the UK.
Passport valid for at least six months.
The consulate does not guarantee approval. Final decision is with the foreign ministry. Do not buy non-refundable tickets first.

stay.note: Days of stay are set by the DGM at entry.

sources.label: MIREX consulate: country list and visa conditions

routes.name: Business Visa (NS / NM)
routes.summary: For business trips. Simple is one entry valid 60 days. Multiple is valid one year with several entries. Even nationals who get a tourist card need a business visa for business travel.

other: Passport valid for at least six months.
Apply at a Dominican consulate. Final approval is with the foreign ministry.

stay.note: Days of stay are set by the DGM at entry.

sources.label: MIREX consulate: country list and visa conditions

routes.name: Entry facility without a visa (exceptional)
routes.summary: An exceptional permission for people who need a visa but can't get one in time. Stay is no more than 7 days. The official page has no separate transit visa rules.

other: Exceptional cases only. Ask the nearest Dominican consulate.

routes.name: Labor Temporary Residence (RT-3)
routes.summary: One-year residence permit for people working in the DR under an employment contract. Enter first on a business visa with work purposes (NM1), then apply to the DGM.

other: Multiple Business Visa (NM1) and a recent entry stamp.
One-year or open-ended contract notarized and sealed by the Ministry of Labor.
Passport valid at least 6 months, apostilled birth certificate and criminal record, DGM-approved guarantee policy and medical exams.

steps: Get the NM1 visa at a Dominican consulate.
Register on personal.migracion.gob.do and pick the service.
Deposit originals in person at the DGM, pay the fees and file.
documents: Notarized work contract sealed by Ministry of Labor
routes.processing: 90 calendar days, per the DGM page.

routes.name: Ordinary Temporary Residence (RT-9)
routes.summary: One-year residence permit for foreigners who plan to settle in the DR. You need a residence visa (RS) first, then apply to the DGM. Renewed yearly. After five years you can apply for permanent residence.

savings.note: Minimum bank balance. RD$150,000 if married to a Dominican.

other: Residence visa (RS) and an entry stamp dated after the visa.
Dominican bank certificate and statement for proof of funds.
Passport valid at least 6 months, apostilled birth certificate and criminal record, DGM-approved guarantee policy and medical exams.

steps: Get the RS residence visa at a Dominican consulate (valid 60 days, one entry).
Register on personal.migracion.gob.do and pick the service.
Deposit originals at the DGM within 30 days of arrival.
routes.processing: 90 calendar days, per the DGM page.

routes.name: Student Permit (E-1)
routes.summary: One-year student permit, renewable yearly for up to six years. You need an E student visa first and proof of enrollment at a registered school.

other: Student visa (E) from a Dominican consulate.
Proof of admission or enrollment at a registered school.
DGM-approved health insurance for the study period.
Proof of money for tuition and living costs.
Passport valid at least 6 months, apostilled birth certificate and criminal record, medical exams.

stay.note: Renewable annually for up to six years.

steps: Get the E visa at a Dominican consulate.
Register on personal.migracion.gob.do and pick the service.
Do the medical exam within three days of paying.
routes.processing: 90 working days, per the DGM page.

routes.name: Permanent Residence (RP-1)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for people who completed five years of annual RT-9 renewals. Apply through the DGM portal.

other: Five years of residence with annual RT-9 renewals completed.
Passport valid at least 18 months and current temporary residence card.
Proof of financial solvency, Dominican criminal record certificate, medical exams.

steps: Register on personal.migracion.gob.do and pick the service.
Deposit originals with copies within 30 days of entering the DR.
Do the medical exam within three days of paying.
routes.processing: Not stated on the DGM page.
